summary: We have developed a game that has programming as its main capability. The user accesses the ship's monitoring system through a terminal located on the main screen, which tracks changes in pressure, the module's stability, its probability of failure, and so on. There will happen some system fault that need the user to resolve urgently.
details:
This project is thought out as a space mission simulation for curious people or students who want to experience it first hand. They handle a terminal to control various parameters in the different phases of the mission. For example, in the launching phase, they choose from one of the missions suggested in the terminal and opt for a destination and a ship to complete such objective (if possible); they also need to perform maintenance of the ship while it's in space.

The intended use for this project is to train the attention and the ability to perform under stress. There will be events with countdown during the voyage, such as repairing a damaged system, which will require the user to access the terminal and insert the proper commands, thus also making them comfortable with the systems that uses more prominently.

In order to develop this game, we cooked ourselves a programming language named Lego. It's a simple language combining the best of Python, C and JavaScript, with support for file management, Machine Learning and web development. As for the visual pictures, we used some spacecrafts from NASA to depict the different ships that should be used depending on the mission.

When thinking of making a game, we considered existing games that focus on the planning more than the experience. We wanted something different and more fresh, that is why we came up with this BrainSpace Overflow, a game in which you rely on rigorous decision making simulating real space travels while also following a clear learning curve so that anyone with passion can start and learn to their heart's content.
